summary: Paired range lights on the St. Marys River's Hay Lake Channel, first lit in 1895; the 1907 towers now stand in two Michigan museums.

light.note: Range lights put in operation 30 Sep 1895 per the Board's 1896 narrative; the Board's list of lights established in the year gives 5 Oct 1895 for the two range lights (see events). The 1907 towers replaced the 1895 pair (LighthouseFriends).

structures.note: 1907 front tower now on the grounds of the DeTour Passage Historical Museum, De Tour Village.
1907 rear tower now at the Les Cheneaux Historical Museum, Cedarville.
Modern tower carrying the front light today.
Modern tower carrying the rear light today.
Brick oil house near the modern lights; built 1898 or 1899 (see events).

access.note: The US Lighthouse Society archive lists the range as not open to the public. The two museum sites: grounds open, towers closed (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Front tower at DeTour Passage Historical Museum (De Tour Village); rear tower at Les Cheneaux Historical Museum (Cedarville). Grounds open, towers closed.

events.note: Range lights (rear and front, on the Hay Lake Channel) put in operation 30 Sep 1895 (Board narrative, FY1896); the Board's list of lights established gives 5 Oct 1895 for the two range lights. Not resolved.
Seven skeleton iron towers built for the channel under contract with the Indiana Bridge Company; the Board does not name the range's towers.
Towers modified: focal planes 40 ft (front) and 54 ft (rear) above lake level.
Oil house built and 310 ft landing dock built out (Board's fiscal year ended 30 June 1899; LighthouseFriends dates the oil house to 1898).
New white cylindrical steel towers first exhibited 1 Dec 1907; pile foundations laid 1906.
Foundations for the Frechette Point and Six Mile Point ranges rebuilt by the close of the fiscal year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The range was first lit in 1895. The Board's narrative puts the lights in operation on 30 September 1895; its list of lights established in the year gives 5 October 1895 for the two range lights. Both dates are stated in the story; the record does not settle which is the first lighting. The record's 1907 'built' date is the replacement pair described by LighthouseFriends, first exhibited 1 December 1907.

notes_for_editor: 1) The FY1895 Board volume (archive.org annualreportlig00boargoog) has a covering letter dated November 9, 1895 that prints 'the fiscal year which ended on June 30, 1896'. The title page reads 'For the fiscal year ended June 30, 1895', and the contents (list of members on June 30, 1895; spring 1895 contracts) show it is the FY1895 report. The story footnote uses 1895; the letter's 1896 is a misprint in the source. 2) Focal heights disagree: Board FY1896 p.145 gives 40 ft (front) and 54 ft (rear) above lake level for the 1895 towers; the archive's record (Source: LL-1901) gives 54 ft and 82 ft above water for the same 1895 towers; LighthouseFriends gives 28 ft and 47.5 ft for the 1907 pair that replaced them (not the same towers). The story states the first two as disagreeing and says the LighthouseFriends figures are for other towers. 3) Tower material: the Board's FY1896 p.144 says the channel's seven towers were skeleton iron and gives no range-tower names; the archive lists the 1895 range towers as steel. Whether the range towers were among the seven is not stated anywhere read; the story says the material is not settled. 4) Oil house year: LighthouseFriends says 1898; the Board's entry is in the report for the year ended June 30, 1899 (p.168). Not treated as a conflict. 5) Richard L. Mitchell's line is as the archive prints it (laborer, '(-1913)'); not checked against NARA registers. The front-range people page (showPeople/9829) prints no names. 6) Chronicling America search for 'Six Mile Point' with 'lighthouse' and with Michigan papers, 1895-1915, returned no lighthouse coverage (four unrelated hits). No newspaper account used. 7) First-lighting dates: the Board's narrative (FY1896 p.144) gives 30 September 1895 as the date the lights were put in operation; the Board's list of lights established in the year (FY1896 p.9, printed as 'Six-Mile Point Range, Hay Lake...') gives 5 October 1895 for the two range lights. Both dates are in the story. The record's first_lit (1895) is kept. 8) The 1909 attendant is unnamed in LighthouseFriends. 9) The record's 'inactive' status conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 'today the lights are shown from modern towers'; check the Coast Guard list before changing it. 10) The Commissioner passage (FY1922 report, printed p.44, 'foundations for structures at Frechette Point and Six Mile Point Rangos have been rebuilt') is read from the bound 1915-1922 volume; its place in the FY1922 report is confirmed by the fiscal-year headings nearby. 11) Rowlett directory and other secondary lists were not read for this story. 12) Page checks: FY1895 p.155 from the running head 'LIGHT-HOUSE BOARD. 155' before the paragraph; FY1896 pp.144-145 from the 'REPORT ... 145' head; FY1896 p.9 from the 'REPORT ... 9' head before the list entry; FY1899 p.168 from the index (Six Mile Point, Mich 34,168); Commissioner p.44 and Bulletin 1922 p.29 from the page index and the PDF page.
